Bhudhi generates tasks with zero knowledge of the outside world. A user building a content business gets the same task wording whether TikTok just launched a new feature or their industry just collapsed. EIS runs as a background worker that researches the user's goal and domain weekly, stores structured intelligence, and injects it into task generation. Bhudhi's tasks go from generic to market-aware.

EIS uses Bhudhi via TriggerRouter only. It does NOT call any external search API unless one is already wired. It uses the Anthropic model's knowledge for now. EIS never mutates blueprints, signals, or conditions. It only produces intelligence objects that task generation reads. Read all files before touching anything.

— PIS — PREDICTIVE INTELLIGENCE + BIS BEHAVIORAL UPGRADE

Bhudhi reacts to what already happened. It has no foresight. PIS gives Bhudhi the ability to predict dropout, burnout, plateau, and scaling readiness from signal patterns before they fully arrive. BIS detects behavior patterns in isolation — but those patterns are not being fed back into task generation or Bhudhi prompts. This prompt builds predictive intelligence and upgrades behavioral awareness.

PIS does not override signals or conditions. It produces advisory prediction objects only. BIS writes behavior patterns — Control Engine and TaskGenerationEngine read them. Neither system forces a condition change directly. Read all files before touching anything.

Deterministic Scoring Rules — No AI Required
Calculate scores from existing DB data. Apply these exact rules:
condition = danger OR nothingness for 5+ days → 0.8. Signal trend = declining for 2 consecutive windows → 0.5. Otherwise → 0.2
behavior_pattern FATIGUE_RISK with severity HIGH → 0.8. cognitive_load_score > 0.8 for 3+ days → 0.7. Otherwise → 0.2
condition = stability for 21+ days with no power movement → 0.6. No milestone in 30 days → 0.3. Otherwise → 0.1
condition = affluence AND momentum >= 7 → 0.9. condition = power AND momentum >= 5 AND burnoutRisk < 0.4 → 0.6. Otherwise → 0.1
If fewer than 3 signal snapshots → LOW. If 3-6 → MEDIUM. If 7+ → HIGH
dropoutRisk > 0.7 → RECOVERY_MODE. burnoutRisk > 0.7 → REDUCE_LOAD. scalingReadiness > 0.7 → SCALE_READY. plateauRisk > 0.6 → INCREASE_INTENSITY. else → MAINTAIN

After deterministic scoring, if confidence is MEDIUM or HIGH only, call Bhudhi via TriggerRouter with trigger type PREDICTIVE_ANALYSIS to get human-readable primaryRisk and primaryOpportunity strings. If confidence is LOW → skip Bhudhi call, use fallback strings.

STEP 4 — BUILD MINIMUM BIS PATTERN DETECTION
Check if BehaviorPatternEngine or PatternLearningEngine is a real implementation. If it is a stub, build these 4 minimum detectors:
If 3+ orders in the last 7 days had feedback submitted more than 2 hours after order creation → write DELAY_PATTERN with severity MEDIUM.
If 3+ consecutive orders of difficulty "hard" or "very_hard" received FAILED or PARTIAL_ACCEPTED feedback → write DIFFICULTY_FAILURE with severity MEDIUM.
If completion_rate dropped more than 30% from the prior 7-day window AND weighted_score dropped more than 2 points → write FATIGUE_RISK with severity HIGH.
If a specific task_type (e.g. "analyze", "research") has been skipped or failed 3+ times in the last 14 days → write TASK_TYPE_AVOIDANCE with the task type as the subject.
Call these 4 detectors from the SignalWorker after signal snapshot is created (they run after every feedback cycle).
